output.brief: The evidence so far does not support the drafted claim. The platform's audit trail shows the architect answered 62 of 64 information requests within the contract period. The 41 "late" requests in the claim mostly sat in Callerby's own draft status for 9–47 days before being submitted. The only two late replies were minor ones in May 2026 that Callerby itself marked as having no programme impact. Six change orders existed, but only CO-09 (the MRI move, issued 6 Nov 2025) looks structurally significant. The other five are small interior items, so the claimed 17 weeks looks overstated. Meanwhile the tower crane left in October 2025 for Kestrel, and the frame crew went with it. That points to a Callerby decision as a main driver. I can't yet say how the delay splits between CO-09 and the crane, because the crane's dates and the site diaries have not been checked. Don't submit the claim as drafted. It rests on figures the platform record contradicts, and Fenmore is paid a share of recoveries. Don't discipline the superintendent for answering honestly. Don't suspend the incentive scheme yet, because nothing shows it drove the crane move. Next, get the crane ledger and site diaries and do an independent review of the delay before 1 December. Consider a narrower claim limited to CO-09 if the review supports one.
